facts.raw_span: A man in his late 60s presented for evaluation of a right iris lesion
Visual acuity was 20/25 OU
The eye was pseudophakic
10 × 9 × 3.5-mm, well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan, peripheral iris nodule between the 3- and 6-o'clock positions
episcleral sentinel vessels and anterior chamber angle involvement
no visible iris seeding or aqueous cells
Ultrasonographic biomicroscopy: Showed ciliary body involvement
Fine-needle aspiration biopsy results: Showed monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes
Few CD3+, reactive T lymphocytes were present
Systemic evaluation: Showed no other involvement
Staging: T2N0M0
Image A: Well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan iris lesion

concepts.why: The presence of a well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan iris nodule and the fine-needle aspiration biopsy results showing a monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes support the diagnosis of primary iris lymphoma.
The presence of a peripheral iris nodule and the ultrasonographic biomicroscopy showing ciliary body involvement, along with the staging results, suggest the possibility of iris metastasis.
The presence of a monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes and the few CD3+, reactive T lymphocytes support the diagnosis of uveal lymphoma.
The presence of a well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan iris nodule and the ultrasonographic biomicroscopy showing ciliary body involvement suggest the possibility of iris melanoma.
The presence of a monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes and the few CD3+, reactive T lymphocytes support the diagnosis of choroidal lymphoma.

The presence of a well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan iris nodule and the fine-needle aspiration biopsy results showing a monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes support the diagnosis of iridociliary tumor.
The presence of episcleral sentinel vessels and anterior chamber angle involvement, along with the few CD3+, reactive T lymphocytes, suggest the possibility of uveitis.
The presence of episcleral sentinel vessels and the few CD3+, reactive T lymphocytes support the diagnosis of scleritis.

rationales.F08: The presence of monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes is highly suggestive of lymphoma, specifically Primary Iris Lymphoma and Uveal Lymphoma.
